conflict.description: He pleads for fairness: 'At least let me say something wrong first before you...' (captioned 'LET' around this point) -- the tension is the imbalance between the accusing look and his desire to actually be heard before being blamed, mirrored visually by the two characters frozen at opposite ends of the seesaw, neither side moving or breaking eye contact.

punchline.description: The sentence lands on '...convict me' -- escalating a petty relationship side-eye into courtroom language, which is the comedic twist: he's being 'tried' for a crime he hasn't committed yet. Dialogue ends exactly at 8.754s.

ending.description: A silent beat: both characters hold their deadpan expressions on the seesaw with no further dialogue, letting the punchline breathe before the shot resolves into the series outro card over the same static frame.
